lungs.title: EIB Interval Warm-Up
lungs.summary: High-intensity interval and variable-intensity warm-ups reduced the post-exercise FEV1 fall most consistently; continuous warm-ups didn't reach significance (Stickland 2012 SR, 7 RCTs). About half of asthmatics get a refractory period (Mickleborough 2007). Protection window ~2–4 h. It's an adjunct — keep using your inhaler per your doctor's plan.

items.name: Interval Warm-Up
items.dose: 5 min easy + 6 × 30 s hard / 30 s easy (HR peaks ~170–180), 10–20 min before the main effort
items.why: Triggers a mild, controlled airway response early so the main effort hits a refractory window.

items.name: Cold/Dry Air Buffer
items.dose: Neck gaiter over mouth/nose on cold days
items.why: EIB is driven by airway drying/cooling; warmer, wetter air reduces the trigger.

lungs.title: Norwegian 4×4 (weekly)
lungs.summary: One session per week. Max HR estimated ~200–205.

items.name: 4 × 4 min intervals
items.dose: 85–95% HRmax ≈ 172–195 bpm; 3 min active recovery ≈ 120–140 bpm
items.why: Time at high heart rate is the VO2max stimulus; 4-min bouts give ~2–3 min in-zone each.

lungs.title: Zone 2 + Nasal Breathing
lungs.summary: Zone 2 builds aerobic base; nasal-only breathing is a simple pace governor and warms/humidifies air.

items.name: Zone 2
items.why: Mitochondrial/aerobic base → faster recovery between sprints, points, rounds.

items.name: Nasal breathing at low intensity
items.dose: All easy runs, walks, cooldowns
items.why: If you can't stay nasal, you're above Zone 2. Nose conditions air before it hits the lungs.

lungs.title: Box Breathing (pre-session)
lungs.summary: Downshifts the threat state before training so the nervous system releases range and speed.

items.name: Box Breathing
items.dose: 4 rounds of 4 s in / 4 s hold / 4 s out / 4 s hold, seated
items.why: Slow breathing raises vagal tone; calmer system = less protective gripping.

lungs.title: Breathing Retraining
lungs.summary: Cochrane (2020, 22 studies): breathing exercises probably improve quality of life and hyperventilation symptoms, with little effect on lung function. Buteyko-specific evidence is a handful of small trials → adjunct only, never a replacement for medication. No mouth taping (asthma). Breath holds only seated or walking — never in water, while lifting, or driving.

items.name: Reduced-Volume Nasal Breathing
items.dose: 5 min daily, seated: breathe in and out through the nose, slightly less air than you want
items.why: Reduces over-breathing pattern linked to symptoms.

items.name: Control Pause (seated)
items.dose: After a normal exhale, hold until first urge to breathe; log seconds weekly
items.why: Simple trend marker of breathing comfort; stop at first urge, never strain.

vision.title: Why vision training (honest grade)
vision.summary: Zhu 2024 meta (22 studies): perceptual-cognitive training effect in real games 0.65 vs 1.51 in the lab — transfer is real but smaller. Generic 'brain games' show no far transfer (Fransen 2024). So: keep drills short and sport-specific — use real balls, real distances, real reactions.

vision.title: Daily Eye Drills (3–5 min)
vision.summary: Eyes are the first link of the kinetic chain. Slow eyes, slow everything.

items.name: Saccades
items.dose: 3 × 20 s jumping eyes between two targets ~1 m apart, head still
items.why: Faster target acquisition — reading a jab or a serve.

items.name: Smooth Pursuit
items.dose: 2 × 30 s tracking a moving pen/ball in a figure-8, head still
items.why: Keeps the ball locked in on long flights (baseball, tennis).

items.name: Peripheral Awareness
items.dose: 2 × 30 s: stare at a fixed point, call out fingers held at the edges
items.why: Seeing the hook coming, the cutter, the open teammate.

items.name: Near-Far Shifts
items.dose: 2 × 20 shifts between a card at arm's length and a far wall target
items.why: Fast refocus between paddle distance and the opponent.

vision.title: Object-Approach Tracking (fear of the ball)
vision.summary: Threat suppression: the brain must learn incoming objects are safe before it releases speed and range. Progress safe → hard.

items.name: Soft Ball Toss to Face Line
items.dose: 2 × 20 — partner tosses a soft/foam ball at your face line; watch it all the way, catch it
items.why: Repeated safe exposures downshift the flinch.

items.name: Progression
items.dose: Foam → tennis ball → closer distance → faster; move up only when you stay relaxed
items.why: Graded exposure keeps the nervous system out of threat mode.

skills.title: Daily Skill Rotation (5–10 min, pick 2–3)
skills.summary: Short, daily, varied. Builds hand-eye, balance and fine coordination you never developed.

items.name: Juggling
items.dose: 3–5 min (2 balls one hand → 3 balls)
items.why: Hand-eye timing and peripheral tracking.

items.name: Wall-Ball
items.dose: 3 × 30 s: switch hands each catch; then one eye closed
items.why: Bilateral hand-eye + depth judgement under challenge.

items.name: Single-Leg Stand Eyes Closed
items.dose: 3 × 20–30 s per side, barefoot
items.why: Forces foot/vestibular balance; feel the tripod foot. Weekly test metric.

items.name: Reaction Ball
items.dose: 3 × 30 s off a wall
items.why: Unpredictable bounces train fast reactions without fear.

items.name: Cross-Body Coordination
items.dose: 2 × 30 s opposite hand-to-knee taps, then skips
items.why: Contralateral rhythm underpins running, punching, throwing.

items.name: Slow-Motion Sport Movements
items.dose: 2 × 5 reps (swing, punch, throw) at 10% speed
items.why: Lets your brain map the hips-lead sequence before you speed it up.

items.name: Eyes-Closed Walking
items.dose: 2 × 10 steps on a line (clear space)
items.why: Proprioception + smooth gait without visual crutch.

recovery.title: Sleep
recovery.summary: Sleep is a training variable. Mah 2011: extending sleep improved sprint time and shooting in college basketball players (n=11 — small, so grade B).

items.name: 9 h target
items.dose: Same bedtime ±30 min; screens off 30 min before
items.why: Growth, recovery, reaction time and mood all ride on it.

items.name: Morning daylight
items.dose: 5–10 min outside within an hour of waking
items.why: Anchors circadian rhythm → easier sleep at night.

recovery.title: Food (recomp, never a cut)
recovery.summary: Eat at maintenance or above. Track waist, photos and strength — not scale loss.

items.name: Protein
items.dose: ~1.6 g/kg/day (Morton 2018) ≈ 90–100 g/day at 125–135 lb, across 3–5 meals
items.why: Captures most of the muscle-building benefit; total matters more than exact timing.

items.name: Close the post-training gap
items.dose: A protein meal within a couple of hours after training
items.why: Avoids a long gap; not a magic window.

items.name: Enough dietary fat + carbs
items.dose: Don't undereat; fast metabolism means extra snacks
items.why: Fuel for training and normal hormone production.

recovery.title: Natural Hormones — Lifestyle Only
recovery.summary: Sleep, eat enough, adequate dietary fat, stay out of extreme leanness. No 'T boosters', no supplement stacks.

items.name: Supplements
items.dose: None by default. Creatine has the strongest evidence base of any sports supplement — decide with a parent/doctor.
items.why: You're a minor; food and sleep first.

recovery.title: HRV-Guided Intensity (Garmin)
recovery.summary: If HRV is well below your 7-day average (or sleep was short), the app auto-switches to 'Cooked': lower volume, keep power crisp.

items.name: Morning check
items.dose: Paste resting HR, HRV, sleep into the app daily
items.why: Adjusts load to readiness instead of guessing.

recovery.title: Cold Exposure Timing
recovery.summary: Cold water right after lifting blunted long-term muscle and strength gains (Roberts 2015). Fine after games or conditioning.

items.name: Rule
items.dose: No ice baths after lifting days; OK after games/conditioning
items.why: Inflammation after lifting is part of the growth signal.

running.title: XC Running Economy
running.summary: Baseline ~8:22/mile @ ~173 bpm avg. Goal: same HR, faster pace.

items.name: Cadence 170–180
items.dose: Use a metronome or beat-matched playlist
items.why: Shorter ground contacts, less overstriding and braking.

items.name: Beat-Synced Music
items.dose: Playlist at your cadence BPM
items.why: Synchronous music lowered oxygen cost and extended time to exhaustion in elite triathletes (Terry 2012).

items.name: Scripted Self-Talk
items.dose: 3 phrases you say at hard moments ('drive the arms', 'you've done this', 'smooth and fast')
items.why: Motivational self-talk extended endurance ~18% and lowered RPE (Blanchfield 2014).

items.name: Interval Warm-Up for Airways
items.dose: 6 × 30 s hard / 30 s easy before races and hard runs
items.why: EIB protection window (Stickland 2012).

items.name: Pogo Hops Before Runs
items.why: Primes ankle stiffness → better elastic return per stride.

items.name: Heavy Legs + Plyos
items.dose: 2 × week strength + jumps
items.why: Strength + plyometrics improved running economy (Balsalobre-Fernández 2016).

looks.title: V-Taper & Proportion
looks.summary: Recomp at maintenance or surplus. Wider lats + lateral delts + upper chest = V-taper. Track waist, photos, strength — not scale loss.

items.name: Lats
items.dose: Pull-ups/rows 10–14 hard sets/week
items.why: Width from behind and front.

items.name: Lateral Delts
items.dose: Lateral raises 8–12 sets/week, last set lengthened partials
items.why: Shoulder width — biggest V-taper lever.

items.name: Upper Chest
items.dose: Incline press 30°, 6–9 sets/week
items.why: Fills the upper chest line.

looks.title: Neck, Forearms, Calves, Posture
looks.summary: Small areas that make a lean build look strong — and neck matters for boxing.

items.name: Neck
items.dose: 2–3 × week: isometrics 2 × 15 s each direction, progress to light resisted curls
items.why: Thicker neck + chin durability.

items.name: Forearms
items.dose: Hammer curls + farmer carries
items.why: Grip for grappling, forearm thickness.

items.name: Calves
items.dose: 2 × week, 10–15 reps, bottom stretch pause + lengthened partials
items.why: Lengthened partials favored for gastrocnemius (Kassiano 2023).

items.name: Posture
items.dose: Face pulls + Y-T-W 2 × week
items.why: Shoulders back = looks wider and taller.

looks.title: Pump on Demand (10 min)
looks.summary: Metabolite sets right before you want to look pumped. Arms down after (don't hold them up) to keep blood in.

items.name: Push-Ups
items.why: Chest, triceps, front delts fill fast.

items.name: Lateral Raises
items.dose: 3 × 15–20 light, 20 s rest
items.why: Shoulder width pops.

items.name: Curls
items.dose: 3 × 15–20 light, 20 s rest
items.why: Arm size.

items.name: Finish
items.dose: Drink water, arms hang relaxed
items.why: Fluid + gravity hold the pump.
